claims.claim: Legacy public apps can no longer be created as of June 23, 2026
claims.quote: As of June 23, 2026, legacy public apps can no longer be created.

claims.claim: Create-app guide asks for HubSpot CLI v7.6.0
claims.quote: Make sure you're using v7.6.0 of the HubSpot CLI before proceeding.
claims.correction: Version number is as of this fetch; it is a pinned page value that may move.

claims.claim: Authenticate CLI with hs account auth
claims.quote: authenticate it with your account using the `hs account auth` command.

claims.claim: hs project create, choose App, prompts for distribution/auth (OAuth for multi-account)
claims.quote: When prompted to select the base contents of your project, select **App**. ... select whether you want to use OAuth for the ability to authenticate multiple accounts, or opt for a static token
claims.correction: Distribution (marketplace vs private) prompt wording itself was not returned verbatim; auth prompt confirmed.

claims.claim: Distribution/auth choices live in app-hsmeta.json; Marketplace distribution requires OAuth
claims.quote: The `distribution` field in your app schema allows you to configure how you want to distribute your app / If you choose this option, ensure that you set the `type` within the `auth` property to `oauth`
claims.correction: Can be upgraded from unverified to verified. Quote 2 is the marketplace option text; paraphrase-level for 'Marketplace requires OAuth'.

claims.claim: At least one HTTPS redirect URL, http://localhost allowed for testing
claims.quote: Each app must have at least one auth redirect URL, and it must use HTTPS. / The only exception is that `http://localhost` is allowed for testing.

claims.claim: requiredScopes/optionalScopes/conditionallyRequiredScopes; at least one scope; minimum read
claims.quote: Each app must include at least one scope, and the installing user must grant these scopes to successfully install the app. / At a minimum, your app must include the `read` scope

claims.claim: Change uid in top-level app-hsmeta.json to a unique value before upload
claims.quote: give a unique name to represent your new app. / UIDs are used as a unique identifier for all your project's components and features.
claims.correction: Quotes confirm unique uid; the exact 'top-level app-hsmeta.json before uploading' wording is paraphrase only.

claims.claim: hs project upload uploads and triggers a build
claims.quote: run the `hs project upload` CLI command to upload your project to your HubSpot account and automatically trigger a new build.

claims.claim: hs project open, Auth tab, copy Client ID and Client secret
claims.quote: In the terminal, run `hs project open` from within your local project directory / Under *Client credentials*, copy the *Client ID* and *Client secret* from your new app

claims.claim: Install in developer test account or standard account from the Distribution tab
claims.quote: On the *Distribution* tab, next to *Test installs*, click **Add test install(s)**.
claims.correction: Developer-test vs standard account wording not returned verbatim (paraphrase only).

claims.claim: Send user to app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize with client_id, scope, redirect_uri then exchange code for access and refresh tokens
claims.quote: The refresh token will be used to get a new access token when the current one expires. (authorize URL shown in code sample 'https://app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize')
claims.correction: Was U/unverified; now readable on the 2026-09 token page (not the legacy S1 page). Add this URL as a source.

claims.claim: Development > App Listings > Create listing; 7 tabs; Submit for review
claims.quote: The app listing wizard has seven tabs of information to fill out: ... Click **Submit for review** in the top right.
claims.correction: Tab names (Listing info, App details, Pricing, App features, Support info, Testing info, Review info) were returned by the fetch.

claims.claim: At least 3 active unique installs, unaffiliated production accounts, last 30 days
claims.quote: your app must have at least three active, unique installs. / Active installs are the number of unique HubSpot production accounts, unaffiliated with your organization
claims.correction: The '30 days' was reported as 'over the past 30 days' by the fetch summary; exact sentence not returned verbatim (paraphrase only for 30 days).

claims.claim: OAuth only, support contact, live Terms/Privacy URLs, public setup guide
claims.quote: your app must use OAuth as its sole authorization method. / You must include at least one support contact method. / URLs for your app's Terms of Service and Privacy Policy must be live and up-to-date.
claims.correction: Setup guide: 'A link to publicly available setup documentation specific to your HubSpot integration.'

claims.claim: Manual review by Ecosystem Quality team; one app at a time; Technology Partner Program Agreement
claims.quote: App listing submissions are manually reviewed by the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team. / you can only submit one app at a time for approval.
claims.correction: Agreement: 'you must review and agree to the terms in HubSpot's Technology Partner Program Agreement.'

claims.claim: Initial review within 10 business days; whole process no more than 60 days from time feedback is shared
claims.quote: the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team will complete an initial review within 10 business days. / The entire app review and feedback process should take no more than 60 days from the time feedback is shared.

claims.claim: Listing-process page itself gives no review timeline
claims.quote: The HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team will review your submission and follow up via email when the app has been approved or rejected.
claims.correction: Only timeline on that page is for unpublish requests (10 business days).

claims.claim: Marketplace: request only needed scopes and use all requested scopes at install
claims.quote: only request scopes your app needs.
claims.correction: 'Use all requested scopes at install' half is paraphrase only.

claims.claim: Example scopes crm.objects.contacts.read and .write on create-app page
claims.quote: sample app-hsmeta.json lists "crm.objects.contacts.read" and "crm.objects.contacts.write" under requiredScopes
claims.correction: Fetch summary description of the sample file (not a prose sentence); can be upgraded from U to V.

claims.claim: hs project dev starts local development; localhost allowed redirect
claims.quote: you can run `hs project dev` to start developing your app locally. / It's already set up to work with `https://localhost:3000/oauth-callback` as the redirect URL
claims.correction: Note the sample redirect is https://localhost:3000/oauth-callback.

claims.claim: Create configurable test account from Development menu; 'Add test install(s)'; tick unverified-app checkbox, click Connect app
claims.quote: On the *Distribution* tab, next to *Test installs*, click **Add test install(s)**. / In the dialog box, review the app's requirements, then select the **checkbox** and click **Connect app**.
claims.correction: 'Add test install(s)' on Distribution tab is on S3 (create-an-app), not S5. S5 only has the checkbox/Connect app dialog for customers; it does not say the checkbox is for 'unverified app' and says nothing on configurable test accounts. Re-attribute and drop unverified wording and test-account creation unless another page is found.

claims.claim: Development > App Listings > Edit draft > Preview runs a test install flow
claims.quote: Run through a test version of the installation process.
claims.correction: The sentence is on S5 (Preview the install flow section), not S7. S7 has no Preview/Edit draft text. Re-attribute source to S5; the 'Edit draft' menu path is unsupported.

claims.claim: Certification: 6 months listed, 60+ active installs, API success >95%, verified domain, demo video, security assessment, response within 10 business days; optional
claims.quote: Your app must be listed in the HubSpot Marketplace for at least six months. / Your app must have at least 60 active, unique installs to qualify for and retain certification. / Maintain an average success rate above 95% across all activities. / HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team responds to app certification requests within 10 business days.
claims.correction: Numbers confirmed. Two parts wrong/unsupported: (1) security assessment is not universal: 'Your app will be subjected to an additional security assessment if it includes a browser extension.' (2) The page does not state certification is optional (unsupported). Also verified domain: 'Be associated with a verified domain.' and demo video: 'HubSpot will not review your app unless you submit a demo video' confirmed.

claims.claim: Legacy OAuth guide: a domain is required, IP addresses unsupported
claims.quote: You also must use a domain, as IP addresses are not supported.
claims.correction: Can upgrade the domain half from U to V.

claims.claim: redirect_uri must exactly match configured value
claims.correction: Not stated on legacy OAuth page or the 2026-09 token page (only 'The app's set redirect URL.' and 'this URL must use https in production'). Keep as unknown. Max number of redirect URLs also not stated.

claims.claim: Exact access-token lifetime unknown
claims.quote: The `expires_in` field specifies how long the access token will last (in seconds).
claims.correction: No fixed number found; official guidance is to read expires_in from the token response. Reword unknown accordingly. (A 1800s figure was not seen on a page I read, so do not state it.)

claims.claim: Only Super Admins or Marketplace-access users can install
claims.quote: Users installing apps in their HubSpot account must either be a Super Admin or have HubSpot Marketplace Access permissions.
claims.correction: Page is the legacy OAuth guide; 'install fails' consequence is paraphrase only. Applies to legacy docs; new-platform page not checked.

claims.claim: Unverified-app banner; one verified domain per account; DNS changes up to 48 hours; Marketplace-listed apps do not need it
claims.correction: Cited S5 has no unverified-app, domain verification, DNS or 48-hour text (fetched twice). Search surfaced https://developers.hubspot.com/changelog/developer-identity-for-hubspot-apps (not read). Remove or re-source.

claims.claim: Incomplete listings revert to Draft; unsupported platform versions cannot be listed; classic CRM cards not allowed
claims.quote: failure to meet these requirements will cause your listing to be set to Draft mode only / apps using that version cannot be listed in the HubSpot Marketplace / your app cannot use classic CRM cards, as they are no longer supported as of June 16, 2025
claims.correction: All three are true but are on S6 (listing requirements), not S7 (listing-your-app), which has none of them. Re-attribute to S6 and upgrade to verified. Draft mode applies to failing the requirements, not literally 'incomplete fields'.

claims.claim: Test installs on own accounts need no review; certification is separate
claims.correction: No page read states test installs need no review or that certification is a separate optional process. Soften to inference.

claims.claim: Marketplace listing needs 3 real installs first
claims.quote: your app must have at least three active, unique installs.

missing: Classic CRM cards are not supported: 'your app cannot use classic CRM cards, as they are no longer supported as of June 16, 2025' (listing requirements page); also apps on an unsupported developer platform version cannot be listed.

Token responses include expires_in: 'The `expires_in` field specifies how long the access token will last (in seconds).' Developers should use it instead of hardcoding a lifetime (https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/latest/authentication/manage-oauth-tokens).

Install-flow page notice: 'After October 26, 2026, all apps listed on the HubSpot Marketplace that wish to make changes to the app listing' (sentence truncated in fetch; read the page at understand-app-install-flow for the full rule). Also the create-app sample uses https://localhost:3000/oauth-callback as the redirect.
